items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I had a similar experience with Juan Tizol of the Duke's band.

ctx.x: Yeah, I went backstage, (inaudible) "I can blow better than you. Why did you give me a solo?" Pulled a knife. Of course, I saw the fire ax. It was lucky I heard about him cutting Cab Calloway; so I found out where the fire ax was. Because he didn't pull his knife (inaudible). (Inaudible). I had a similar experience with Juan Tizol of the Duke's band.
Wonderful story. And you had a fire ax then, as a matter of fact.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: he told Celley to throw him out; to give him his two weeks notice and pay him off and let him go.

ctx.x: upstairs in my dressing room, and I was so nervous, I was crying, you know? And he came up there, and the manager was there at the door of my dressing room, and when he came up there, he still wanted to keep saying something; I don't know it was what, but he wanted to keep on arguing about it with me.

And, I didn't respond or anything; I stayed right like that in my dressing room, and Celley was there trying to hold him back, you know? So, Duke came over -- I don't know how, but he told Celley to throw him out; to give him his two weeks notice and pay him off and let him go.
So he came back again -- he said, 'Juan, you made me lose my job' and so forth, and I said, 'Well, I can't help it -- you started it'. That was about the end of it.
